reflection.summary: Two shift experiments (dr=3,dc=3 and dr=5,dc=5) show agreement nearly unchanged from baseline (deltas of -0.00019 and -0.00041), providing no evidence for a spatial offset at these tested shifts. However, these are low-information tests because only two points on the shift surface were sampled; a peak at a different offset or a flat surface cannot be distinguished. The residual gap to the 0.75 threshold remains large (~0.213). H001 remains plausible but unconfirmed; H002, H003, and H004 remain active. Next, run a systematic shift scan over a range of offsets to map the agreement surface, and compute cloud-fraction bias to test H003.

reflection.summary: Three experiments (shifts of 3 and 5 pixels, and a horizontal flip) all produced agreement within 0.0006 of the baseline (~0.537), with no informative variation. This strongly rules out a large spatial offset or orientation mismatch (H001), but the tested shifts were small and sparse, so a larger systematic shift scan is still needed to fully exclude H001. The flat agreement surface also suggests that temporal mismatch (H002) and threshold calibration (H003) are plausible, but no direct evidence yet distinguishes them. Data quality (H004) remains possible given the 31% invalid-pixel fraction, but no spatial analysis has been performed. The no-fault hypothesis (H005) remains viable because the observed agreement may be scientifically valid for this comparison. Next, run a systematic shift scan over a wider range (e.g., dr,dc in -10..10) to map the agreement surface, and compute cloud-fraction difference and mismatch spatial distribution to test H003 and H004.
